captions.instagram:
How is cheese made?

Cheese is milk with nine-tenths of it taken away. Watch one enzyme snip the hairy coat off the milk's protein, cut and cook the curd, press it, salt it, and age it in a cave until bacteria blow the holes.

→ Milk is 87% water. Cheese keeps the protein and fat and lets the water go.
→ Ten litres of milk make about one kilogram of hard cheese.
→ Rennet's enzyme, chymosin, cuts the hairy coat off every casein micelle.
→ Bald micelles link up with calcium, and the whole vat sets into curd.
→ Cutting lets the whey out. Small cubes cooked hot make hard cheese, and big cubes make soft cheese.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/cheeseclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How is cheese made? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Cheese is milk with nine-tenths of it taken away. Watch one enzyme snip the hairy coat off the milk's protein, cut and cook the curd, press it, salt it, and age it in a cave until bacteria blow the holes.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/cheeseclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/cheeseclear

In this video:
• Milk, minus the water. Milk is about 87% water carrying fat, casein protein, lactose and a little whey protein.
• Rennet cuts the hairs. Casein lives in tiny balls called micelles, each coated with kappa-casein hairs that keep them apart.
• Cut, cook and drain. Cutting the curd opens doors for the whey.
• Press and salt. Pressing knits loose curd into one solid block.
• Flavour is made in the cave. A young cheese is bland and rubbery.
• One family, many cousins. How much water is left and how long it ages place every cheese on one map.
